author: ValWood
body:
Yep, this is a hangover from the old "contributes_to" usage.
Fixed to GO:0005246   [ JSON](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/GO:0005246/complete)
calcium channel regulator activity

Note SGD ortholog annotated as a channel not a regulator
https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000005235
tagging @suzialeksander 


SGD annotation is
Stretch-activated Ca2+-permeable cation channel; required for Ca2+ influx stimulated by mating pheromones and some abiotic stresses; sensor of compressive mechanical stress; N-glycosylated membrane protein of the ER and plasma membrane; interacts with Cch1p; oligomerizes; is an alpha2/delta-like protein and participates in the generation of stretch-activated Ca2+-permeable cation channel activity when expressed in mammalian cells
so I wonder if this subunit is the sensor activity part?

author: hattrill
body:
Actually, looking at this again, I think that there is some major divergence between fungi and metazoans.

The[ InterPro IPR055288 NALCN channel auxiliary factor 1/2](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR055288/) / [PMID:32494638](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/32494638#abstract)  characterise this as a sodium leak channel - permeable to monovalent cations and blocked by divalent cations (e.g Ca2+!):
"The resulting NALCN channel complex is constitutively active and conducts monovalent cations but is blocked by physiological concentrations of extracellular divalent cations." "NALCN represents the sole member of a distinct branch of the four-domain ion channel family, which includes the extensively studied voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels (NaVs and CaVs)" - perhaps this is where the difference lie and the IBA propagation family needs to be reexamined? @marcfeuermann 

From  https://europepmc.org/article/MED/33273469 "FAM155 [aka NALF1 in humans] is the homolog of NLF-1 in C. elegans, which is required for the membrane localization of NALCN[12](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/33273469#CR12). It is proposed that the interaction between NALCN and FAM155 is similar to the interaction between yeast calcium channel Cch1 and its regulator Mid1"

Evolution of the Mid1 superfamily is explored in "[Ancient association between cation leak channels and Mid1 proteins is conserved in fungi and animals](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3945613/)"  

So for Mid1, etc perhaps the most accurate terms to propagate 
MF GO:0005261 monoatomic cation channel regulator
BP  GO:0098659 inorganic cation import across plasma membrane 
for 
PTN001813414
TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEIN FAM155 (PTHR15819)


(note for me For the channel itself, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5459923/ indicates that Dmel na is a soduim leak channel)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hello, 
Thank you for all this information. PAINT is running slowly right now, but I was able to review the annotations for this family. I removed all annotations based on _S. cerevisiae_ and _S. pombe_ and annotated FAM55A/NALF1 based on PMID:32494638.
I've added the **BP GO:0098659 inorganic cation import across plasma membrane** as suggested.
However, **GO:0005261** corresponds to **monoatomic cation channel activity** not to **monoatomic cation channel regulator** which does not seem to exist.
Instead, I used **GO:0016247 channel regulator activity**
Best regards,
Marc.
